# docs/drift-detection.md | Drift detection and change freeze | Rules | updated 2026-02-25

# docs/dynamodb-data-model.md | DynamoDB single-table data model | DynamoDB single-table data model | updated 2026-05-12
Per ADR-003 (accepted 2026-05-06): one table, `relay-deliveries`, composite keys.

# docs/dynamodb-data-model.md | DynamoDB single-table data model | Keys | updated 2026-05-12
| Item | PK | SK |
|---|---|---|
| Delivery | `CUST#<customer_id>` | `DEL#<created_at>#<delivery_id>` |
| Attempt | `CUST#<customer_id>` | `DEL#<created_at>#<delivery_id>#ATT#<n>` |
| Endpoint | `CUST#<customer_id>` | `EP#<endpoint_id>` |
| Idempotency key | `CALLER#<caller_arn>` | `IDEM#<key>` (TTL 24 h) |

# docs/dynamodb-data-model.md | DynamoDB single-table data model | Access patterns | updated 2026-05-12
1. Create delivery and first attempt: one transaction.
2. Deliveries for a customer in a time range: query PK with SK between.
3. Delivery by id: GSI `by-delivery-id`.
4. Pending deliveries for the worker: GSI `by-status` on `status#next_attempt_at`.
5. Endpoints for a customer: query PK with SK begins_with `EP#`.
6. Idempotency lookup: get item.

Six patterns, matching the six Relay has had for three years. A new pattern means a new GSI, which is the trade-off recorded in ADR-003.

# docs/gateway.md | API gateway integration | Timeouts | updated 2026-03-18
The integration timeout on every Relay route is **10 seconds** (decided 2026-03-16). It is a round number above the p99 of `POST /deliver` at intake, 1.8 s. The synchronous `wait=true` mode can exceed it; that mode is being removed and the timeout is not sized for it.

# docs/gateway.md | API gateway integration | Retries | updated 2026-03-18
Retries on `POST /deliver` are **disabled** (decided 2026-03-30): a delivery is not idempotent yet, and a retried request can reach the customer twice. Read routes retry up to two times.

# docs/gateway.md | API gateway integration | Retry budget | updated 2026-03-18
When retries are enabled on a route they are capped by a retry budget: the share of retried requests among all requests to the route over a one-minute window. Above the budget the gateway stops retrying until the window clears. The value is set per route in the gateway policy, not in Relay.

# docs/idempotency.md | Idempotency keys on /deliver | Idempotency keys on `/deliver` | updated 2026-05-20
Decided 2026-05-18. To make `POST /deliver` safe to retry, callers send an `Idempotency-Key` header, a UUID chosen per logical delivery. Relay stores the key with the delivery for 24 hours; a second request with the same key returns the original delivery id and does not deliver again.

# docs/idempotency.md | Idempotency keys on /deliver | Rollout | updated 2026-05-20
- From **2026-06-01** the header is mandatory. For two weeks requests without it are accepted and logged; after 2026-06-15 they are rejected with 400.
- Keys are scoped per caller (`X-Caller-Arn`), so two services may reuse a UUID.
- Same key, different body: 409.

# docs/idempotency.md | Idempotency keys on /deliver | Why | updated 2026-05-20
Gateway retries on `/deliver` were disabled on 2026-03-30 because a retried delivery could reach a customer twice. Once every caller sends keys, retries can be enabled at the gateway with a limit and a budget set in the gateway policy.

# docs/idempotency.md | Idempotency keys on /deliver | Storage | updated 2026-05-20
Keys live in the deliveries table with a TTL of 24 hours. In the DynamoDB design the key is the sort key of the `IDEMPOTENCY#` item under the caller's partition.

# docs/poc-dynamodb-report.md | "PoC-1 report: DynamoDB designs" | Results | updated 2026-05-01
| Design | Read p99 | Write p99 | Monthly cost at projected volume |
|---|---|---|---|
| DocumentDB (baseline, current) | 9 ms | 14 ms | $5,200 |
| DynamoDB multi-table (4 tables) | 11 ms | 9 ms | $5,100 |
| DynamoDB single-table | **4 ms** | 8 ms | **$3,200 (-38%)** |

Multi-table loses on reads because the delivery-by-customer pattern needs two queries and a join in the application. Single-table serves every pattern with one query or one GSI.

# docs/poc-dynamodb-report.md | "PoC-1 report: DynamoDB designs" | Recommendation | updated 2026-05-01
Single-table. The cost is query flexibility: every pattern is designed up front and a new one requires a new GSI. Relay's patterns have not changed in three years.

Reviewed 2026-05-04; objection from the architect on flexibility recorded in ADR-003.

# docs/retries-dlq.md | Delivery retries through SQS and the DLQ | Mechanism | updated 2026-08-27
- `relay-intake` writes the delivery and sends one message to `relay-deliveries`.
- `relay-deliver` posts to the customer. On failure or timeout it throws; SQS redrives with exponential backoff: 30 s, 2 min, 10 min, 30 min, 2 h.
- After **5 attempts** the message goes to `relay-deliveries-dlq`; an alert fires and the delivery is marked `failed`.
- Gateway retries on `POST /relay/deliver` are **off**; a gateway retry would enqueue twice.

# docs/secrets.md | Secrets handling | Parameters | updated 2026-09-10
| Parameter | Type | Rotation |
|---|---|---|
| `/relay/prod/signing/<endpoint_id>` | SecureString | on customer request |
| `/relay/prod/docdb/credentials` | SecureString | **overdue**: last rotated January 2026; must be rotated before DocumentDB decommission |

# docs/secrets.md | Secrets handling | Cost of the rule | updated 2026-09-10
About 100 ms on a cold start, hidden by provisioned concurrency on `relay-deliver`. Rotation is a parameter update followed by a redeploy.

# docs/secrets.md | Secrets handling | Access | updated 2026-09-10
Functions get `ssm:GetParameter` on their own prefix only. `describe` on the stack no longer reveals anything.

# docs/serverless-architecture.md | Serverless architecture | Serverless architecture | updated 2026-08-12
Per ADR-006 (2026-08-05). Relay runs on Lambda.

```
caller --SigV4--> API gateway --> intake Lambda --> SQS (deliveries)
                                                      |
                                        delivery Lambda (provisioned concurrency)
                                                      |
                                   customer endpoint   +--> DynamoDB (relay-deliveries)
                                                      +--> DLQ after 5 attempts
```

# docs/serverless-architecture.md | Serverless architecture | Functions | updated 2026-08-12
| Function | Trigger | Memory | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `relay-intake` | gateway `POST /relay/deliver` | 512 MB | validates, writes the delivery, enqueues; returns 202 |
| `relay-deliver` | SQS `relay-deliveries` | 1024 MB | signs and posts; provisioned concurrency (sizing open, owner Ivan) |
| `relay-query` | gateway `GET /relay/*` | 256 MB | reads |

# docs/serverless-architecture.md | Serverless architecture | What changed from EKS | updated 2026-08-12
- Intake is asynchronous: `POST /deliver` returns 202 with a delivery id; the synchronous `wait=true` mode is gone.
- Retries move from the gateway to the queue (see [retries-dlq.md](retries-dlq.md)).
- The gateway integration timeout matters only for intake; it is being revisited for Lambda.
- Secrets handling is under security review.

# docs/serverless-architecture.md | Serverless architecture | Infrastructure | updated 2026-08-12
Everything is in the `compute` and `gateway` nested stacks (SAM transform). Networking inputs still come from Terraform through SSM.

# docs/slo.md | Relay SLOs | Relay SLOs | updated 2026-01-28
Decided 2026-01-26.

| Indicator | Objective | Window |
|---|---|---|
| Delivery latency, p95: from `POST /deliver` accepted to the first delivery attempt sent | **2 s** | 5 minutes |
| Delivery success rate: deliveries that reach the customer endpoint after all attempts | **99.5%** | calendar month |
| `GET /deliveries/*` latency, p95 | 500 ms | 5 minutes |

The latency SLO measures Relay, not the customer: it ends when the first attempt is sent, not when the customer answers.

# docs/slo.md | Relay SLOs | Error budget | updated 2026-01-28
99.5% success leaves 0.5% of deliveries per month. Half of the downtime budget implied by that is reserved for planned work such as the gateway cutover and the compute migration; the other half is operational. If the operational half is spent, feature work on Relay stops for the rest of the month.

# docs/slo.md | Relay SLOs | What counts | updated 2026-01-28
Gateway timeouts and 5xx from Relay count against success. Customer endpoints returning 4xx after all attempts count as delivered-but-rejected and do not count against the SLO.

DocumentDB serves Relay's deliveries table. Read p99 has climbed to 9–11 ms at peak and cost grows with volume. Relay has six fixed access patterns. PoC-1 compared a DynamoDB single-table design with a multi-table design on a production-shaped dataset.

# adr/ADR-003.md | ADR-003: Replace DocumentDB with DynamoDB using a single-table design | Decision | updated 2026-05-06 | status Accepted
DynamoDB single-table design, chosen on PoC-1 results (p99 read 4 ms vs 11 ms; 38% lower cost at projected volume).

Objection recorded from Timur Aliev.

metadata.doc_title: ADR-003: Replace DocumentDB with DynamoDB using a single-table design
metadata.author: Denis Orlov

text:
# adr/ADR-003.md | ADR-003: Replace DocumentDB with DynamoDB using a single-table design | Consequences | updated 2026-05-06 | status Accepted
Single-table gave p99 read 4 ms against 11 ms multi-table and 9 ms DocumentDB, and 38% lower cost at projected volume. Every access pattern must be designed up front; a new query means a new index. The architect's objection on query flexibility is recorded. Migration is backfill, dual write, then cutover; a dry run on a production snapshot is required before the backfill.

# confluence/architecture.xhtml | Relay architecture | Relay architecture | updated 2026-03-12
Relay accepts delivery requests from product services and posts signed webhooks to customer endpoints. This page describes the runtime shape; the API is in the repository under docs/overview.md.

# confluence/architecture.xhtml | Relay architecture | Runtime | updated 2026-03-12
relay-api (3 replicas) and relay-worker (6 replicas) run on the shared EKS cluster. Callers reach the API through the API gateway since March 2026. The system of record is DocumentDB (relay-prod-docdb, one writer, two readers).

# confluence/architecture.xhtml | Relay architecture | Infrastructure code | updated 2026-03-12
Application stacks are CloudFormation (relay-<env> root with nested stacks); the networking module is being moved last. See CloudFormation migration guide.
